name: Curtain Call
tagline: You love every minute. Even the last one, if you let it.
epigraph: The Bloody Mary once had a politer name, and no ice at all.
glassware: a stemmed wine glass (about 250-300 ml), chilled, no ice
language_row: Wren's Resonance on reading v4: ready. The fear is kept narrow by the courage scene and by the feeling that arrives mid-best-part. "His last book" implies his death, gently, and y4 stands between it and y5. No "one more", no morning after, no brunch. The 4-gram check is clean against every pour; five echoes were cleared in v1 (*Off Duty*, *Standing By*, *Fair Measure*, *As It Was* twice). No "go first" (*Off Duty*), "allowed" (*Four Shares*) or "apologise" (*The Other Berry*, *Still Yours*). The he/his warnings in yours 1–4 are Gaige, and Lauryssen once, never the guest (accepted by Wren, round 6). History about 37%. ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/crosby-gaige.md`: *Oxford Companion to Spirits and Cocktails* GAIGE, CROSBY pdf 861, BLOODY MARY pdf 291–293, RED SNAPPER pdf 1624; Crosby Gaige's cocktail guide (copyright 1941; archive.org OCR of the 1946 fifth printing, p. 57, Lauryssen's Red Snapper); *Journal of the American Dietetic Association* review (August 1942) for the 1941 imprint; UP wire obituary (*Kingston Daily Freeman*, 8 March 1949); *Saturday Review* and Kirkus (1949) for *Dining with My Friends*; *Print* (Summer 1941) and Paul Shaw for the barn press and the fine-press years. Drink: Gary Regan, *The Joy of Mixology* pdf 249, 373; *Cocktail Codex* pp. 221, 225; *Flavor Matrix* tomato pdf 244 (consulted, set aside). Room notes: `work/lover-explorer/`.
names_note: **Curtain Call**, the room's pick (all three, from round 4): the moment at the end of a show when people cheer, the ending loved. It makes no claim about his curtains or his count. Also considered: *Lights Up* (it sounds like "start" at a bar and spends whoYouAre's best line), *While It's Good* (the position said twice), *Full Table*, *House Lights*. *Encore* was left out because at a bar it means "one more".
open_items: **His death is implied, gently:** "His last book is called *Dining with My Friends*" (Crown, 1949, published after he died on 8 March 1949). No date, no cause, and never that he saw it published. Wren chose it as the truest "the people don't vanish" on the record. The book itself is lending-only and hasn't been read; its contents run as dinners (OCR of the contents page).

**The drink starts from Lauryssen's St. Regis Red Snapper in Gaige's 1941 guide** (2 oz tomato juice, 2 oz vodka, Worcestershire, salt; the OCR cuts off after that). Ours is equal parts at 45 ml, with the Worcestershire (`gluten` on the safe side) and any heat (`spice`) taken out, and a splash of manzanilla, fresh lemon and celery salt put in. It's never "his recipe". "Served straight up" rests on *Joy* pdf 249; the shake is Regan's method (pdf 373).

**Tomato** is *The Other Berry*'s surprise; here it stays savoury, with no surprise in it. The `tomato_juice`, `manzanilla` and `celery_salt` values are unsourced (Tomás added them, safe-side, none of the vetoes). The sweep across the plausible tomato range barely moves the numbers.

**Legends and inferences kept out:** the gin Red Snapper (DeGroff, via O'Hara 1999: carded as legend L3); *Joy*'s 1945 (a later printing, our inference); "lost them all" (a 1976 auction catalogue); the herb garden (not found); Beebe (never named); "150 curtains" (Oxford's figure is a career "encompassing 150 plays"); the crash closing his theatre (he produced in 1935).
**Closing line** went through four versions (rounds 4–6, two crossings). v1.4 turns whoYouAre's "long before anyone reaches for a coat" around, and stays off y5's two steps.
